title: Your UnEmbedding Matrix is Secretly a Feature Lens for Text Embeddings
task: Improving text embeddings from LLMs by filtering high-frequency token subspace
key_results: EmbedFilter achieves superior zero-shot performance with 40-50% dimension reduction while preserving embedding quality across multiple LLM backbones
comments: Simple linear transformation approach is elegant but limited to post-hoc refinement of embeddings rather than addressing root causes during training

hypotheses.hypothesis: Unembedding matrix encodes frequent-token subspace that suppresses semantic information in embeddings
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: filtering this subspace improves downstream task performance

title: MMAE: A Massive Multitask Audio Editing Benchmark
task: Comprehensive evaluation of instruction-based audio editing systems
key_results: Current systems achieve <5% Exact Match Rate with 0% performance on mixed-modality complex tasks; benchmark includes 2,000 samples across 7 audio modalities with 17,741 verifiable criteria
comments: Rubric-based evaluation is more rigorous than typical benchmarks but human-agent curation may introduce bias in task difficulty distribution

hypotheses.hypothesis: Current audio editing systems struggle with precise execution in complex, mixed-modality tasks
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: EMR drops to 0% on mixed-modality tasks versus <5% on simpler tasks

title: SoCRATES: Towards Reliable Automated Evaluation of Proactive LLM Mediation across Domains and Socio-cognitive Variations
task: Evaluating proactive LLM mediators across diverse conflict scenarios and socio-cognitive variations
key_results: Topic-localized evaluator reaches 0.82 alignment with human experts; strongest mediator closes only ~1/3 of consensus gap; performance varies sharply by socio-cognitive axis
comments: SoCRATES addresses realistic multi-domain evaluation but 0.82 inter-rater alignment suggests remaining ambiguity in mediation quality assessment

hypotheses.hypothesis: Socio-cognitive factors (emotional reactivity, cultural identity) significantly impact mediation effectiveness
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: performance varies sharply across adaptation axes despite similar strategic posture

title: AnchorWorld: Embodied Egocentric World Simulation with View-based Evolution Customization
task: Egocentric world simulation with customizable view-based evolution
key_results: AnchorWorld outperforms state-of-the-art baselines with improved spatio-temporal geometric consistency; auxiliary exogenous supervision enhances spatial grounding
comments: Use of 3D motion as primary interaction modality is grounded but limiting; unclear how well approach generalizes beyond scripted scenarios with predefined anchors

model_io.model: Video diffusion model with auxiliary supervision

hypotheses.hypothesis: Auxiliary exogenous viewpoints improve spatial grounding of human-world interactions in egocentric simulation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: inclusion of exogenous supervision yields significant performance improvements

title: Direct 3D-Aware Object Insertion via Decomposed Visual Proxies
task: Pose-controllable object insertion with 3D awareness via decomposed visual proxies
key_results: DIRECT enables interactive 3D pose manipulation while maintaining visual quality; outperforms previous methods in both geometric controllability and visual fidelity
comments: Decomposition into appearance/geometry/context pathways is intuitive but requires user 3D pose specification, limiting automation potential

hypotheses.hypothesis: Separate conditioning pathways for appearance, geometry, and context avoid feature entanglement
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: decomposition preserves reference appearance while following pose and adapting to scene context

title: SubtleMemory: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Relational Memory Discrimination in Long-Horizon AI Agents
task: Fine-grained relational memory discrimination in long-horizon AI agents
key_results: Current systems weak on relational memory discrimination; 1,522 evaluation instances over 1,090 relation-controlled memory-variant sets reveal distinct capability gaps across preservation, retrieval, and reasoning stages
comments: SubtleMemory addresses important but understudied problem; construction method via latent semantic artifacts is sophisticated but may not capture all real-world memory complexity

model_io.model: Long-running AI agents with memory modules

hypotheses.hypothesis: Current memory systems struggle to preserve and utilize fine-grained relations between memories during downstream tasks
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: distinct capability gaps observed across memory preservation, retrieval, and reasoning stages

title: When Tools Fail: Benchmarking Dynamic Replanning and Anomaly Recovery in LLM Agents
task: Evaluating LLM agents' dynamic replanning and error recovery under tool failures
key_results: Tool perturbations degrade performance across all models; Perturbation Recovery Rate drops ~37% under implicit semantic failures; fault-tolerance improves 3.66x slower than basic task execution
comments: ToolMaze's two-dimensional perturbation taxonomy is principled but implicit semantic failures remain poorly characterized for targeted improvement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Implicit semantic tool failures are harder to recover from than explicit failures due to agent over-trust
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: PRR plummets to ~37% reduction under implicit scenarios vs. explicit

title: GENEB: Why Genomic Models Are Hard to Compare
task: Diagnostic benchmarking of genomic foundation models across diverse functional tasks
key_results: Model rankings vary sharply across task categories; scale provides only modest and inconsistent gains; architectural and pretraining alignment outweigh parameter count; aggregate leaderboards are unstable
comments: GENEB's 40-model, 100-task evaluation is comprehensive but probing-based protocol may miss domain-specific capabilities not detectable through frozen representations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model scale provides consistent performance gains across genomic tasks
hypotheses.result: Refuted: scale gains are modest and inconsistent; architectural and pretraining choices matter more

title: LIMMT: Less is More for Motion Tracking
task: Data-centric optimization of physics-based humanoid motion tracking
key_results: Training with <3% of AMASS yields better tracking than full dataset; quality defined by physics feasibility, diversity, and complexity
comments: LIMMT's findings on data quality are valuable but generalization to other motion tracking tasks and embodiments remains unclear

hypotheses.hypothesis: High-quality motion data with good physics feasibility and diversity enables better optimization trajectories than larger low-quality datasets
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: <3% high-quality data outperforms full AMASS dataset

title: Watch, Remember, Reason: Human-View Video Understanding with MLLMs
task: Understanding video through multimodal LLMs with watching, remembering, and reasoning abilities
key_results: Comprehensive framework for analyzing video MLLMs across perception, memory, and reasoning; identifies challenges in spatio-temporal perception, efficient long-video processing, and streaming understanding
comments: Survey provides useful conceptual framework but lacks quantitative benchmarks for comparing different paradigms; focuses on taxonomy over empirical evaluation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Effective video understanding requires integrated capabilities across watching (perception), remembering (memory), and reasoning stages
hypotheses.result: Supported: framework identifies distinct challenges at each stage

title: UniSHARP: Universal Sharp Monocular View Synthesis
task: Universal monocular view synthesis across diverse camera systems
key_results: UniSHARP extends SHARP to panoramic, fisheye, and wide-FoV cameras; outperforms alternatives by large margin through ray-based universal representation and unified omnidirectional latent space
comments: Generalization across camera modalities is valuable but evaluation focuses on rendered quality metrics; real-world applicability to extreme distortions unclear

hypotheses.result: Confirmed: ray-based universal representation outperforms camera-specific approaches

title: Robots Need More than VLA and World Models
task: Identifying missing components for robot learning from unstructured behavioral data
key_results: Position paper identifies four critical interfaces: data autolabeling, embodiment retargeting, world-model physics reasoning, and reward inference from video/language
comments: Well-reasoned position but lacks empirical validation; argues against dominant VLA-scaling paradigm but provides limited concrete alternatives

hypotheses.hypothesis: Policy learning alone is insufficient bottleneck; robots need mechanisms to extract supervision from unstructured behavioral data
hypotheses.result: Proposed but not empirically validated in this paper

title: dots.tts Technical Report
task: Continuous autoregressive text-to-speech with semantic-structure preservation and reward-free post-training
key_results: dots.tts achieves state-of-the-art on Seed-TTS-Eval with WERs of 0.94%/1.30%/6.60% and SIM scores of 81.0/77.1/79.5 on zh/en/zh-hard sets; low-latency inference with 85/54ms first-packet latencies
comments: Strong empirical results but AudioVAE design choices and reward-free self-corrective training procedure lack detailed ablation studies

hypotheses.hypothesis: Full-history conditioning and reward-free self-correction improve robustness and acoustic quality in continuous TTS
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: achieves state-of-the-art performance across benchmarks

title: Thinking with Imagination: Agentic Visual Spatial Reasoning with World Simulators
task: Agentic visual spatial reasoning through world simulator interaction and imagination
key_results: Astra improves Gemini-3-Flash from 45.1 to 49.5 on MMSI-Bench; Qwen3-VL improves from 29.8 to 38.8 via RL-trained policy and view-consistency world simulator
comments: Combining world model with agentic reasoning is promising but requires significant compute for RL training; view consistency tuning specifics not fully detailed

hypotheses.hypothesis: Learning when and how to use world simulator imagination improves spatial reasoning over direct answering
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: RL policy learns to selectively invoke simulator when beneficial

title: OpenSkill: Open-World Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
task: Open-world self-evolution for LLM agents without target-task supervision
key_results: OpenSkill bootstraps skill acquisition and verification from open-world resources; achieves best automated pass rates on three benchmarks while satisfying no-supervision constraint; skills transfer across models
comments: Ambitious goal but reliance on documentation/repositories for grounding may not scale to truly novel domains without relevant web resources

model_io.model: LLM agent with skill acquisition and verification modules

hypotheses.hypothesis: Open-world resources can supply both knowledge to learn and self-supervision for skill refinement without target-task annotations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: best automated pass rates achieved under no-supervision constraint

title: Physics in 2-Steps: Locking Motion Priors Before Visual Refinement Erases Them
task: Preserving motion priors in few-step diffusion to maintain physical consistency through denoising
key_results: 2-step generation exhibits better physical consistency than 50-step; PhaseLock improves physical consistency by 6.2 points average while maintaining visual fidelity with 1.06x time overhead
comments: Spectral analysis insight is novel but limited theoretical understanding of why phase degradation occurs; training-free approach is practical

hypotheses.hypothesis: Phase information in diffusion latents encodes motion priors that degrade during extended denoising; extracting and enforcing 2-step phase preserves physical consistency
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: PhaseLock improves physical consistency while maintaining visual quality

title: LLM Explainability with Counterfactual Chains and Causal Graphs
task: Explaining LLM inference through causal graphs constructed from counterfactual chains
key_results: Method discovers class-discriminative human-interpretable concepts and constructs stable causal graphs; MCMC-inspired augmentation enables stable causal discovery with σ-CG
comments: Concept-level explainability is valuable but validation limited to three task types; causal discovery stability not thoroughly benchmarked against alternatives

model_io.model: Concept discovery and causal graph construction system

hypotheses.hypothesis: MCMC-inspired counterfactual augmentation enables stable causal discovery of LLM inference mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: approach yields interpretable causal graphs with good convergence properties

title: PaperFlow: Profiling, Recommending, and Adapting Across Daily Paper Streams
task: Longitudinal scientific paper recommendation with daily profiling, recommending, and adapting
key_results: PaperFlow achieves strongest oracle-based ranking and best blind human-evaluation score; benchmark includes 24 simulated users, 50 daily streams, 1,200 user-day episodes, 20,727 unique papers
comments: Longitudinal evaluation is more realistic than static ranking but simulated users may not capture full complexity of researcher interest evolution

model_io.model: Paper recommendation system with profile/recommend/adapt stages

hypotheses.hypothesis: Longitudinal daily adaptation outperforms static ranking in capturing shifting research interests
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: PaperFlow achieves best performance through multi-signal aggregation and interest drift modeling

title: Socratic-SWE: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Trace-Derived Agent Skills
task: Self-evolving SWE agents via trace-derived skills and closed-loop task generation
key_results: Socratic-SWE reaches 50.40% on SWE-bench Verified after three iterations; consistently improves over baselines under same compute; distilled skills guide targeted task generation
comments: Closed-loop self-evolution is novel but task validation relies on execution without semantic understanding; generalization beyond SWE-bench unclear

model_io.model: SWE agent with skill distillation module

hypotheses.hypothesis: Distilling structured skills from agent traces enables more effective task curriculum than fixed mutation-based generation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: skill-guided task generation improves performance over baselines

title: Stream3D-VLM: Online 3D Spatial Understanding with Incremental Geometry Priors
task: Online 3D spatial understanding from streaming video with incremental geometry priors
key_results: Stream3D-VLM outperforms proprietary and open-source models on 29-task streaming benchmark; Geometry-Adaptive Voxel Compression provides efficient visual token compression; 1M+ online 3D QA pairs generated
comments: Autoregressive streaming formulation is elegant but computational efficiency gains from compression module not quantified in latency terms

hypotheses.hypothesis: Incremental geometry priors and efficient voxel compression enable real-time 3D understanding from streaming video
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: approach outperforms baselines on online and offline 3D tasks

title: When Gradients Collide: Failure Modes of Multi-Objective Prompt Optimization for LLM Judges
task: Analyzing failure modes in multi-objective prompt optimization for LLM judges
key_results: In 6/10 configurations optimization never improves; gradient specificity drops 59% when processing multiple criteria jointly; instruction interference degrades Spearman's rho by -5.3%
comments: Identifies important failure modes but limited exploration of solutions; mainly diagnostic work without proposing fixes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Naive multi-objective textual gradient optimization causes gradient dilution and instruction interference
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: separate pathways and criteria specifications needed

title: HarnessForge: Joint Harness and Policy Evolution for Adaptive Agent Systems
task: Meta-adaptive agent systems via joint harness-policy co-evolution
key_results: HarnessForge improves Qwen3 models by up to 12% over baselines; harness-policy co-evolution outperforms harness-only and policy-only approaches across five diverse benchmarks
comments: Separating harness and policy adaptation spaces is conceptually clean but complexity of optimization landscape for joint evolution not fully characterized

hypotheses.hypothesis: Joint harness-policy co-evolution outperforms independent optimization of execution structure or reasoning policy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: gains up to 12% demonstrate importance of compatibility

title: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
task: Self-improving AI through simultaneous harness and weight updates
key_results: SIA achieves 56.6% improvement on LawBench, 91.9% runtime reduction on GPU kernels, 502% improvement on RNA denoising over baseline
comments: Combining harness and weight updates is promising but limited to three domains; convergence properties of coupled updates not analyzed

hypotheses.hypothesis: Simultaneous harness and weight updates enable better self-improvement than sequential or single-lever approaches
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: combined approach outperforms baselines on all three domains

title: Towards Retrieving Interaction Spaces for Agentic Search
task: Constructing bounded interaction spaces for agentic search via retrieval
key_results: RISE matches pure-shell DCI baseline at 78% accuracy with 1/4 per-query cost; at 1M documents RISE-BM25 reaches 81% vs. DCI's 60% accuracy with fewer failures
comments: Interaction space concept is intuitive but BM25 boundary construction is simplistic; scaling to massive corpora may require more sophisticated space design

hypotheses.hypothesis: Constructing bounded interaction spaces reduces computational cost while maintaining accuracy compared to unbounded direct corpus interaction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: RISE achieves comparable accuracy with 1/4 per-query cost

title: Entropy as a Structural Prior: How a Log-Barrier on DiT Belief Space Drives Musical Diversity and Development
task: Entropy-based loss weighting for music generation via log-barrier on diffusion model belief space
key_results: Eisbach log-barrier improves thematic development, acoustic differentiation, and textural diversity vs. unweighted training; parameter-free approach derived from output entropy
comments: Novel insight on confidence weighting in supervised diffusion but limited to music domain; generalization to other modalities unclear

hypotheses.hypothesis: Entropy-based log-barrier weight improves diversity by dampening gradients on low-entropy (flat) samples while preserving high-contrast ones

title: LayerRoute: Input-Conditioned Adaptive Layer Skipping via LoRA Fine-Tuning for Agentic Language Models
task: Input-conditioned adaptive layer skipping for agentic language models via LoRA
key_results: LayerRoute achieves 12.91% skip differential with only 1.10M trainable parameters; tool calls skip 15.25% FLOPs while planning steps skip 2.34%; quality improves via LoRA adaptation
comments: Fine-grained per-input routing is novel but benefit limited to small models; scaling laws with model size not explored

title: Towards Human-Like Interactive Speech Recognition With Agentic Correction and Semantic Evaluation
task: Interactive speech recognition with agentic correction and semantic evaluation
key_results: Iterative interaction consistently reduces semantic errors across multilingual/NER/code-switching benchmarks; S^2ER metric better captures semantic improvements than token-level metrics

title: How Far Can Chord-Symbol Time-Series Adaptation Carry Genre Identity? Capabilities and Boundaries in Multi-Genre Chord-Symbol Modeling

key_results: LoRA and IA3 achieve highest gains (+2.89 to +3.61 macro points); method choice less important than data size; chord symbols alone do not carry complete genre identity
comments: Comprehensive 165-cell ablation across methods and genres is thorough but limited to chord prediction; perceptual evaluation avoided due to evaluation complexity

hypotheses.hypothesis: Small adaptation methods enable comparable genre transfer without full fine-tuning

title: Streaming Video Generation with Streaming Force Control

key_results: StreamForce enables causal force-responsive video generation at 16.6 FPS on single GPU; unified model handles local/global time-varying forces with state-of-the-art adherence and realism
comments: Unified force representation is elegant but training pipeline details sparse; comparison to per-force-type baselines not quantitatively detailed

hypotheses.hypothesis: Unified force representation enables efficient learning across diverse force types vs. separate models
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: single model achieves state-of-the-art with lower parameter count

title: Compress-Distill: Reasoning Trace Compression for Efficient Knowledge Distillation
task: Compressing reasoning traces before knowledge distillation to reduce student verbosity
key_results: Compressed traces reduce training tokens to 12-30% of raw, speed up training 2-7.6x, shorten inference 3-19x; raw traces retain highest accuracy at all scales
comments: Compression offers accuracy-efficiency tradeoff but not free improvement; students on compressed traces retain up to 96% of raw-trace accuracy

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model-compressed traces provide better accuracy-efficiency tradeoff than naive truncation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: compression usually beats truncation especially for smaller students

title: WorldBench: A Challenging and Visually Diverse Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark
task: Evaluating visual diversity and challenging reasoning in multimodal language models
key_results: WorldBench achieves higher visual diversity than existing benchmarks; frontier MLLMs reach only 64% accuracy with significant variance; models perform marginally above chance on diverse concepts
comments: Visual diversity emphasis is valuable but 64% ceiling suggests benchmark may be too hard for fair model comparison; concept taxonomy construction process not detailed

hypotheses.hypothesis: Visual diversity is essential for robust multimodal reasoning; existing benchmarks lack sufficient diversity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: WorldBench achieves higher diversity than alternatives; poor performance suggests gaps remain

title: Parametric Social Identity Injection and Diversification in Public Opinion Simulation

key_results: PSII reduces KL divergence to real-world survey data; significantly improves distributional fidelity and diversity vs. prompt-based approaches; addresses diversity collapse in intermediate layers

outputs: opinion responses from distinct social identities

hypotheses.hypothesis: Injecting parametric demographic representations directly into hidden states preserves social diversity better than prompt conditioning
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: PSII improves KL divergence and diversity metrics

title: Critic-R: Improving Agentic Search using Instruction-tuned Retrievers with Natural Language Introspective Feedback
task: Improving agentic search retrieval via instruction-tuned retrievers with critic feedback
key_results: Critic-R improves retrieval quality and answer accuracy on four multi-hop datasets; inference-time query refinement and automatic supervision from trajectories avoid gold-standard annotations
comments: Closed-loop agent-retriever feedback is intuitive but critic model training itself requires supervision; scalability to very large corpora unclear

hypotheses.hypothesis: Critic model evaluation of agent reasoning enables effective query refinement without gold-standard relevance labels
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: automatic supervision from trajectories improves retrieval quality

title: Augmenting Attention with Exponentially Decaying Memory Improves Query-Aware KV Sparsity
task: Improving query-aware sparse attention via exponentially decaying memory augmentation
key_results: RAT+ memory module consistently improves sparse inference methods (Quest, MoBA, SnapKV) across needle-in-haystack tasks; benefits validated on released checkpoints and continued pretrained OLMo2

title: A chronic whole cigarette smoke extract model reveals redox–mitochondrial adaptation in human lung epithelial and organoid models
task: Model chronic cigarette smoke adaptation in lung epithelium via redox-mitochondrial remodeling
key_results: Chronic WCSE exposure induced coordinated redox-mitochondrial adaptation with reduced apoptosis, enhanced S-phase, fragmented but functional mitochondria, and sustained NRF2 via post-translational stabilization independent of KEAP1; oxidative mutational signatures detected by WES; organoid models recapitulated phenotype
comments: The KEAP1-independent NRF2 stabilization mechanism is intriguing and suggests alternative regulatory pathways (e.g., GSK3β-mediated phosphorylation) merit deeper investigation.

Human lung organoids exposed to chronic WCSE

title: Long-term inhibition of lysosomal glucocerebrosidase activity promotes GPX4 stability and inhibits ferroptosis in dopaminergic neurons
task: Determine how glucocerebrosidase inhibition affects ferroptosis in dopaminergic neurons
key_results: 10-day CBE treatment increased GPX4 protein levels and blocked RSL3-induced ferroptosis in LUHMES cells; effect was transient and reversed by day 20
comments: The transient nature of the protective effect suggests adaptive responses may limit therapeutic utility of glucocerebrosidase inhibition for PD.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Glucocerebrosidase inhibition protects against ferroptosis through GPX4 stabilization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 10-day CBE increased GPX4 and blocked RSL3-induced ferroptosis

title: CUL7-mediated KEAP1 ubiquitination promotes the progression of colon cancer via NRF2 signaling
task: Determine how CUL7-mediated KEAP1 ubiquitination promotes colon cancer via NRF2 signaling
key_results: CUL7 high expression correlated with poor prognosis; CUL7 deletion inhibited proliferation/migration; CUL7 catalyzed K29/K48-linked polyubiquitination of KEAP1, promoting NRF2 stabilization and ROS reduction
comments: The mechanistic link between E3-ligase activity and cancer metabolic reprogramming is well-established, though the specific role of K29 vs K48 linkages in NRF2 stabilization deserves further analysis.

hypotheses.hypothesis: CUL7 promotes colon cancer by ubiquitinating and degrading KEAP1, stabilizing NRF2
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; CUL7 ablation reduced NRF2 signaling and tumor growth; C-terminus of CUL7 is critical for KEAP1 targeting

title: TMEM63B regulates nucleocytoplasmic transport and placental development
task: Determine how TMEM63B regulates trophoblast cell cycle and placental development via nucleocytoplasmic transport
key_results: TMEM63B stabilized nucleocytoplasmic transport (NCT) components; loss of TMEM63B impaired Ran/XPO1 complex and nuclear export of CDKN1A/p21, causing defective trophoblast proliferation and placental dysfunction with perinatal lethality
comments: The coupling of osmo/mechano-sensing to cell cycle regulation via NCT is novel and suggests mechanotransduction plays a central role in placental development.

title: The embryonic origins of site-specific arthritis
task: Identify embryonic origins of site-specific arthritis predilection to proximal interphalangeal joints
key_results: PIP joints had larger synovial volume and enriched PI16+ 'universal' fibroblasts located in perivascular regions and tendon-ligament interfaces; these cells exhibited shared inflammatory response plus cell-type-specific cytokine sensitivity, suggesting spatial-transcriptional synergy promotes inflammation
comments: The perivascular location and in utero stoichiometry of fibroblasts provide developmental explanation for acquired disease predilection, implicating organogenesis in adult disease susceptibility.

model_io.model: Fetal human finger joint tissue (palate and skin)

title: Probiotic intervention mitigates radiation-induced intestinal injury by alleviating oxidative stress in a human gut-on-a-chip
task: Assess probiotic mitigation of radiation-induced intestinal injury using gut-on-a-chip
key_results: Probiotic formulation reduced ROS production and epithelial damage in 8 Gy gamma-irradiated Caco-2 cells; morphological preservation occurred independent of 53BP1 foci reduction

title: Temporal changes in gene regulation during human tissue repair
task: Elucidate temporal gene regulatory mechanisms driving differential healing in oral mucosa versus skin
key_results: Palate exhibited regenerative repair with minimal scarring versus skin; acute injury response characterized by TF-mediated gene repression followed by tissue-specific activation; BATF3 promoted palate-specific cell migration and re-epithelialization but not proliferation

model_io.model: Adult human palate and skin wound models (7-day time course)

title: Canonical autophagy remains inactive in induced pluripotent stem cells and neuronal progenitor cells following DNA damage induced by BPDE or etoposide
task: Investigate whether genotoxic stress activates canonical autophagy in stem cells
key_results: iPSCs and NPCs retained functional autophagy (starvation-induced flux confirmed) but showed no autophagic activation following BPDE or etoposide treatment despite robust DNA damage response (γH2AX, p53)

model_io.model: iPSC lines (iPS11, iPS12) and derived NPCs (niPS11, niPS12)

title: Arsenic exposure promotes retinal pigment epithelium dysfunction and oxidative stress via NF-κB pathway
task: Elucidate how arsenic exposure exacerbates retinal pigment epithelium dysfunction and age-related macular degeneration via NF-κB pathway
key_results: Arsenic at 1 µM (in vitro) or 25 ppm (in vivo) exacerbated NaIO3-induced RPE injury through sustained NF-κB activation; As increased ROS, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis, autophagy dysregulation; NF-κB silencing partially reversed As-induced damage
comments: The multifactorial effects (ROS, mitochondria, autophagy) downstream of NF-κB activation suggest As acts as a stress amplifier rather than a primary trigger.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed; As amplified NaIO3-induced injury and NF-κB activation in both models; NF-κB silencing provided partial protection

title: Effect of 3D-printed co-culture design of mesenchymal stem cells and human umbilical vein endothelial cells on tubular formation
task: Optimize 3D-bioprinted co-culture geometry for endothelial tubular formation
key_results: Three designs tested; BMSC-containing constructs supported CD31+ endothelial networks; adjacent filament constructs achieved comparable network formation to co-printed designs (P<0.05 for tubular surface area); physical proximity sufficient without filament co-localization
comments: The finding that adjacency suffices for tubular induction simplifies bioprinting design while revealing the importance of cell migration distance over spatial organization.

key_results: LSTM and BiLSTM models trained on CVAO (10 years) achieved MFE <0.17; transferred to ASI dataset with MFE <0.16; strong transferability to remote marine regions
comments: Excellent transferability and long-term training window; SHAP analysis reveals inconsistent feature importance across models, limiting mechanistic interpretability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Air-parcel history improves PNSD reconstruction via LSTM temporal modeling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; MFE <0.17 on CVAO with strong cross-site transfer

title: Realization of fermionic Laughlin state on a quantum processor
task: Realize fermionic ν=1/3 Laughlin state on trapped-ion quantum processor
key_results: ν=1/3 fermionic Laughlin state demonstrated on 16-qubit IonQ system with 369 two-qubit gates; correlation hole, bulk-edge correspondence, and topological entanglement entropy verified against exact diagonalization
comments: Landmark demonstration of genuinely fermionic topological order on digital quantum hardware; symmetry-verification error mitigation essential for observable extraction reliability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Efficient variational ansatz can prepare fermionic Laughlin state with topological signatures preserved under noise
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via symmetry-verification error mitigation; strong agreement with benchmarks achieved

title: Layer-number-parity-dependent abnormal magnetic ordering in few-layer CrI3 on N-face AlN substrate
task: Programming layer-parity-dependent magnetic multistates in few-layer CrI₃ via polar substrate
key_results: Odd-layer CrI₃/AlN exhibits distinct magnetic multistates (+5 → –1 → +1 → –5) under field sweep; interfacial hole doping reconfigures ground state to ferrimagnetic order
comments: Novel heterointerface engineering approach with clear parity-dependent effects, though mechanism relies on first-principles predictions rather than direct structural evidence.

outputs: reflective magnetic circular dichroism signal evolution

hypotheses.hypothesis: Interfacial hole doping globally reconfigures odd-layer CrI₃ magnetic ground state
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via DFT; ferrimagnetic order emerges with spatially differentiated interlayer coupling

title: Deep learning-assisted ultrafast ferroelectric domain imaging using atomic force microscopy
task: Accelerate piezoresponse force microscopy via deep learning for ferroelectric domain imaging
key_results: Sequential U-Net with transfer learning recovers high-quality domains from low-SNR images with >50% improvement; enables >390× faster PFM imaging and >67× faster electrostatic force microscopy while maintaining quality
comments: Hardware-agnostic, broadly applicable approach; generalization across lock-in techniques demonstrated but quantitative validation metrics (domain reconstruction error) not detailed in abstract.

inputs: low-quality PFM/EFM images (fast acquisition, low SNR)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Neural network can recover domain structure fidelity from low-SNR lock-in AFM images without hardware modification
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; >50% improvement vs. random initialization; speed-up validated across PFM and EFM modalities

title: Investigation of the guaiazulene–p-chloranil charge transfer complex in solution: a combined spectroscopic and quantum chemical approach
task: Characterize guaiazulene–p-chloranil charge-transfer complex via spectroscopy and DFT/TDDFT
key_results: Strong donor-acceptor binding with Ka=20,830 dm³ mol⁻¹ (absorption) and 43,560 dm³ mol⁻¹ (fluorescence); CT transition energy 1.534 eV (TDDFT) matches experimental 1.537 eV; NIR CT band at 808 nm
comments: Excellent agreement between theory and experiment validating donor-acceptor coupling mechanism; binding constant discrepancy between spectroscopic methods deserves clarification.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Favorable π-orbital overlap between guaiazulene and p-chloranil π* orbitals facilitates strong charge transfer
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via DFT showing efficient orbital alignment and TDDFT predicting CT transition in excellent agreement with experiment

title: Gas capture and selective sensing performance of graphene-like AlNC2 monolayer: a DFT study
task: Evaluate gas adsorption and selective sensing of AlNC₂ monolayer using DFT
key_results: Strong chemisorption for NO₂, SO₂, NO, NH₃; moderate for CO, H₂S; weak for CH₄; reversible adsorption for moderate adsorbates with difficult desorption for strong ones at ambient T
comments: Comprehensive DFT characterization with recovery time analysis; lacks experimental validation of sensing selectivity and actual device integration.

inputs: gas molecules (CO, NO, NO₂, SO₂, NH₃, H₂S, CH₄)

hypotheses.hypothesis: AlNC₂ exhibits selective chemisorption depending on gas molecule electron affinity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; acceptor/donor behavior correlates with gas type; reversibility varies by binding strength

title: Impedance study of the charge leakage phenomenon in ITO-free graphene-super-yellow light-emitting diode
task: Analyze charge leakage in ITO-free graphene/MoOₓ organic light-emitting diode via impedance spectroscopy
key_results: Increased hole injection relative to electron injection; significant hole-electron recombination at graphene-polymer interface responsible for charge leakage; electrical equivalent circuit modeling monitors charge carrier density and leakage
comments: Novel impedance-based method provides interface charge transport insight; limited to one material system, generalization unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hole-electron recombination at graphene-polymer interface dominates charge leakage
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via impedance analysis and circuit modeling

title: Broadband solar energy harvesting and near-perfect thermal emission on a unified stepped-high concentric dual-ring metamaterial
task: Design broadband solar metamaterial absorber with near-perfect thermal emission
key_results: Stepped-height concentric dual-ring TiN absorber achieves 99.27% average absorptivity (150–3000 nm), maintains blackbody-like emission across 373–1500 K, angular independence to 60°
comments: Excellent broadband performance leveraging material stability of TiN; practical high-temperature applications merit experimental validation of thermal cycling durability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vertically graded impedance and multi-resonance coupling enable ultra-broadband absorption
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; synergistic interplay of interband transitions, LSPR, PSR, and guided modes achieved

title: Coupled Geant4–SPICE optimization of a portable CdTe-based alpha detector for environmental radon monitoring
task: Design portable CdTe-based alpha detector for radon monitoring with coupled simulation
key_results: Sensitivity 0.15 cps/(Bq/m³), energy resolution <2% FWHM at 5.49 MeV, response time <15 min over 50–1000 Bq/m³ range
comments: Comprehensive instrument-level design coupling particle transport and electronics modeling; practical environmental robustness validated but limited to bench testing.

title: Enhanced prediction of electric field distribution in lightning protection systems with heterogeneous ground
task: Predict electric field distribution near lightning conductors in heterogeneous ground using COMSOL
key_results: At D/hc=1.5, electric field strength 20% lower than homogeneous case; at D/hc≥3.5, agreement recovers to conductor-less baseline
comments: Practical geometric insights but limited to numerical simulation without experimental validation of discharge behavior.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ground discontinuities significantly affect electric field strength near conductors
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for D/hc<3.5; negligible effect beyond D/hc≥3.5

title: Design and evolution of the tetracycline repressor into sulfonylurea herbicide-responsive gene switches for field crops
task: Engineer TetR-based gene switches responsive to herbicides instead of antibiotics for crop regulation
key_results: Designed TetR mutants achieve low-nanomolar EC50 for sulfonylurea herbicides; functional in tobacco, soybean, maize, rice, and Arabidopsis; siRNA feedback enhances response magnitude and creates partial bistability
comments: Elegant engineering of ligand specificity with crystal structure validation, but field-level stability, pleiotropic herbicide effects on plants, and regulatory acceptance remain practical considerations.

model_io.model: Herbicide-inducible gene switch with siRNA feedback

hypotheses.hypothesis: TetR can be engineered to bind herbicides with high affinity while maintaining operator specificity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; crystal structures reveal extensive herbicide-repressor interactions enabling low-nanomolar EC50

hypotheses.hypothesis: siRNA-mediated repressor feedback amplifies and spatially distributes the herbicide response
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; increases magnitude and creates partial bistability in mammalian cells and plants
